newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to support renewal of Iraq oil-for-food deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to support renewal of Iraq oil-for-food deal.

text.p: The United States will support renewal of the United Nations' oil-for-food programme for Iraq, the State Department said on Tuesday.
Secretary of State Madeleine Albright "has decided that the United States will support the renewal of U.N. resolution 986 and that is the oil for food deal," spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.
The U.N. Security Council is due to vote on the renewal this week, probably Thursday, U.N. diplomats said.

The current deal, which expires on June 7, calls for $2 billion worth of oil sales over six months so Baghdad can buy food and medicine for its people, suffering from sanctions imposed in August 1990 when Iraqi troops invaded Kuwait.
"This agreement benefits the people of Iraq, as it should. It does not benefit in any way the government of Iraq, which does not deserve international support," Burns said.

U.N. Secretary General Kofi Annan has recommended that the oil-for-food deal, which went into effect last December, be renewed for six months. It temporarily waives a U.N. ban on oil sales imposed after the invasion of Kuwait.
Most Security Council members have said they would like to see the agreement approved under current terms or even increased.
U.S. officials said they were working on a straightforward resolution, without complications, on rolling over the plan.
About two-thirds of the oil revenues are for humanitarian supplies, with the remainder earmarked for compensation of Gulf War victims and the costs of destroying Iraq's weapons of mass destruction.
Iraq has complained frequently that the United States has slowed down the council's procedures and delayed goods from reaching the country within a reasonable period of time.
Burns said the U.S. mission to the United Nations had been assured the agreement would be adhered to rigorously and that there would be no "leakage" of funds to the Iraqi government.

"I think we have known that there were some problems in the implementation in the first round, and we think they should be taken care of in the second round, and we've been assured that it will be," he said.
"We will be watching because we will not support this programme if there's any indication that Saddam Hussein is profiting illegally from it."
